hook_text: Accountants have a ten-second trick that tells them instantly if a whole month of receipts was written down wrong.
clip_script: April at a repair shop. Every time money comes in, it goes into the cash receipts journal twice: once in the bank lane, once in the lane that says what kind of money it is. Earned from repairs? Current income. Owner's top-up, storeroom rent, bank interest? Sundry, with a name tag. Even a customer's EFT for a stove repair goes to current income: how money travels never changes what kind of money it is. Month-end: add the current income lane, eighteen thousand six hundred and fifty. Add sundry, twelve thousand six hundred and eighty. Add the bank lane, thirty-one thousand three hundred and thirty. Now the trick: current income plus sundry must equal bank. Eighteen six five oh plus twelve six eight oh: thirty-one three three oh. Match. Rule one line, two lines, done.
visual_style: A whiteboard journal filling in day by day, coins dropping into two lanes, then three column totals with a big plus sign and an equals sign lighting up.
mood: Satisfying and clever, a magic-trick reveal.
pacing: Brisk day-by-day entries, a slow build to the cross-cast, a crisp finish on the ruling lines.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and close off a whole month yourself.
